page: UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-384GB-2xL40S is a KVM-hypervised GPU server powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor. This x86_64 architecture CPU features 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs with a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, supported by 64 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 16 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing 12.0 GB of RAM per core. For acceleration, it bundles two NVIDIA L40S GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a combined 96 GB of VRAM. Local storage is not included in this configuration, and it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier performance, placing in the top 10% for both single-core and multi-core CPU execution via stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark CPU testing. Cryptographic and vector execution capabilities are supported by hardware flags including AVX-512 and VAES. Memory bandwidth is strong, reaching 6364.76 GB/sec for cached reads and 327.05 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. For AI workloads, the dual L40S GPUs achieve top-tier LLM inference speeds on small (135M) models, processing 5508.2 tokens/sec, while maintaining strong top-25% performance on medium (7B) models. Large (70B) model inference falls into the average tier.

Given its high-density hardware profile, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for resource-intensive deployments by consolidating massive parallel compute and memory capacity into a single virtualized instance. The lack of local storage requires external storage integration, which represents a structural tradeoff. This configuration is highly suited for GPU-accelerated workloads such as machine learning model training, medium-scale LLM inference, ray tracing, and high-performance database operations.

The server integrates two NVIDIA L40S GPUs from the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing 96 GB of total VRAM, though it lacks local storage. This hardware profile is highly efficient for consolidating heavy compute tasks, making it a strong fit for machine learning inference, data science, ray tracing, and database operations.
